record.original_question: Let G be a polycyclic group and let phi be an endomorphism of G. The twisted conjugacy search problem asks: given elements w and t in G, with t = a^-1 w phi(a) for some a in G, find such an element a. What is the computational complexity of this twisted conjugacy search problem for polycyclic groups?

evidence.quote: The twisted conjugacy search problems is to find, given a group G and an endomorphism phi, an element a in G such that t = a^-1wphi(a), provided that at least one such a exists.
(2) What is the complexity of the twisted search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is polycyclic if it admits a subnormal series $G = G_0 \trianglerighteq G_1 \trianglerighteq \cdots \trianglerighteq G_n = \{1\}$ with each quotient $G_i/G_{i+1}$ cyclic. Given a polycyclic group $G$ and an endomorphism $\varphi : G \to G$, two elements $w, t \in G$ are said to be twisted $\varphi$-conjugate if there exists $a \in G$ such that
\[ t = a^{-1}\, w\, \varphi(a). \]
The twisted conjugacy search problem is: given $G$, $\varphi$, and elements $w, t \in G$ with the promise that at least one such $a$ exists, compute an element $a \in G$ satisfying $t = a^{-1} w \varphi(a)$.

Determine the computational complexity of the twisted conjugacy search problem for the class of polycyclic groups (e.g., is it solvable in polynomial time, NP-complete, or harder, in terms of natural input size measures such as the length of $w$, $t$ and a description of $\varphi$ relative to a fixed polycyclic presentation of $G$?).
artifact.category_tag: computational group theory / polycyclic group cryptography
artifact.status_search_result: The twisted conjugacy search problem in polycyclic groups underlies proposed authentication schemes and is generally considered hard. Recent work (Tertooy, 2020; sequel 2025) provides algorithms deciding twisted conjugacy and computing Reidemeister coincidence class representatives in polycyclic-by-finite groups under finiteness conditions, but these do not establish a complexity classification of the search problem. Related results show that conjugacy search in some polycyclic groups is at least as hard as subset sum (NP-complete). No source found resolves the precise complexity of the twisted conjugacy search problem for general polycyclic groups, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Algorithms for twisted conjugacy classes of polycyclic-by-finite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Two algorithms determine twisted conjugacy and Reidemeister coincidence class representatives under finiteness assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides algorithms but does not classify computational complexity of the search problem in general polycyclic groups.

status_evidence.title: Algorithms for twisted conjugacy classes of polycyclic-by-finite groups II
status_evidence.snippet: Sequel extending algorithmic treatment of twisted conjugacy in polycyclic-by-finite groups.
status_evidence.claim: Continued algorithmic study indicates the precise complexity remains unsettled.

status_evidence.title: A family of polycyclic groups over which the uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs polycyclic groups whose conjugacy search/decision problems are at least as hard as subset sum.
status_evidence.claim: Standard (untwisted) conjugacy search can be NP-hard, suggesting twisted version is at least as hard, but no definitive classification given.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of Conjugacy Search in some Polycyclic and Matrix Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies restricted conjugacy search in polycyclic groups via discrete logarithm reductions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent complexity studies focus on restricted variants, leaving the general twisted case open.
